HDR.hypothesis: For objects with a matte or rubber surface finish, an anomaly occurs when the smaller object is positioned such that it appears partially outside of the larger one without being fully contained within its boundaries and both objects are of the same shape. For objects with a glossy or metallic surface finish, an anomaly happens when there are multiple objects of different sizes present in the scene and they do not appear to be interacting as expected based on their relative positions, regardless of shape.

For cubes, an anomaly occurs when the smaller cube has a different surface finish than the larger one (one glossy/metallic and one matte/rubber). For spheres, an anomaly happens when both spheres are of similar size but have different surface finishes or when there is no significant difference in size between two spheres with dissimilar surface finishes.

For cubes, an anomaly occurs when the smaller cube has a different shape from the larger object regardless of surface finish and color. For spheres, an anomaly happens when there are multiple spheres or if the single sphere is not centered in the scene.
